title: Write findings that can be checked
statement: Write each finding as one falsifiable problem with its exact location, the offending text word for word, why it matters, a concrete fix and the rechecks that show it fixed.
detail: The reading course's review-evidence format accepts a failure only with one falsifiable problem, exact evidence, why it matters, an exact target, a specific proposed change and named rechecks, and rejects stale, duplicate, vague or unknown results (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/standards/course-json/README.md`, lines 113-117). Its red-team skill reports every count raw, exempted and real, after an all-caps sweep read 392 raw, of which 104 were play-script speaker labels and a skill name; publishing 392 would have cost the finding its standing (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/course-red-team/SKILL.md`, lines 102-106). The skill gives the real number as 284, so the figures as written do not reconcile: 392 less 104 is 288.

evidence.quote: A failure additionally needs one falsifiable problem, exact evidence, why it matters, an exact target object/path, a specific proposed change, a repair-owner skill, and named rechecks.
**Report counts as raw / exempted / real, with the exemption rule stated.**
sweep read 392 raw; 104 were play-script speaker labels and a skill name; the real number was 284.
Report **per lesson**, ranked by severity, and for every finding give:
- what is wrong, in one plain sentence
- a concrete fix (rewritten option, word to gloss, step to reorder)
If a check found nothing, say so rather than padding the report.
Each block is made out of sight and gets a label to cite (`QC-1`, `VE-1`).
four scripted personas (strong, guesser, stuck, adversarial) play the lesson, and any fault is named by block.
A blocking comment must cite an `OJ-*` rule, a mapped `RP-*` criterion, exact artifact locator, and reproducible evidence. Otherwise it is input for future scope, not an invented blocker.
idk, can we propose a series of reasonable how-tos, not just pointing shit out.
And here’s the offline how-to playbook: six concrete proposals, each with example wording, an implementation rule and a test case.
Four separate things, and they are fixed by different people: the script is mostly good; some lines read vague; the delivery feels soulless; and the face may not be needed throughout.
Prefer one verbatim-evidenced finding over five speculative ones.
